name: Humanitarian funding gap
value: WFP cuts Sudan and Gaza aid; no full suspension
summary: WFP says 900,000 people in Sudan have lost food aid over funding cuts and it has halved rations for most in Gaza
state: WFP said on 19 Oct that funding cuts forced it to cut Gaza food assistance by about a third, from 1.6 million to 1.1 million people a month, and halve rations, with $450 million needed to March 2027 (WFP). WFP said in mid-November that a funding shortfall has left about 900,000 people in Sudan without food aid (Asharq). Major ration cuts meet Watch; no large-scale suspension of food or health aid in a famine-risk country was found as of 21 Nov.
for_you: People relying on WFP rations in Sudan and Gaza are most exposed. Further cuts tend to follow when donor pledges lag, usually announced country by country.
rubric_hit: Watch: major ration cuts announced (WFP Gaza, 19 Oct; Sudan 900,000 cut off); no large-scale suspension

sources.title: WFP — Funding cuts force WFP to drastically reduce lifesaving assistance in Gaza
Asharq — WFP: funding shortfall leaves 900,000 Sudanese without aid

why: When appeals go unfunded, food aid and health services are cut first; funding gaps lead famine and displacement by months.
drivers: Donor budgets and aid cuts, new crises competing for funds, access constraints.

rubric.alert: Pipeline breaks forcing large-scale suspension of food or health aid in famine-risk countries.
rubric.watch: Funding more than 10 percentage points behind recent years at the same point, or major ration cuts announced.
rubric.normal: UN global appeal funding in line with recent years; no major ration cuts.
